cover.hook: Anthropic is going public at a $2 trillion target — and it plans to build in Canada.
cover.sub: Plus $1.5M into NWO's forestry accelerator, Scandinavian investors in Thunder Bay, and two major AI model price drops this week.

reelSub: Five AI and funding stories NWO can't ignore this week.
storySub: What this week's AI and funding news means for a Northwestern Ontario business.

items.title: Ontario puts $1.5M into NWO's forestry accelerator
items.body: The province funded the Boreal Springboard through Ontario's Trade-Impacted Communities Program, announced October 8. Up to $40K per NWO forest-business entrepreneur, plus a Soft-Landing stream for outside companies wanting to scale in the region.
items.tease: Next: who came all the way from Scandinavia to look at it.
items.reelLine: $1.5M into NWO's forestry-business accelerator this week.

items.title: Scandinavian investors arrived to scout NWO poplar and white birch
items.body: About 50 delegates including Swedish companies came to Thunder Bay October 5–7 to assess the region's hardwood resources. NOIC, CEDC, and the Bio-Economy Research Centre organized it. No deals — but foreign capital is actively looking at NWO forestry.
items.tease: Next: AI just got dramatically cheaper.
items.reelLine: Sweden came to Thunder Bay to look at our hardwood this week.

items.title: Anthropic cuts API pricing 90% for small-model tasks
items.body: Claude Haiku 5.5 launched October 7 at $0.10 per million input tokens, down from $1. Designed for summarization, classification, and high-volume routines. Anthropic estimates 75% lower workload costs on average.
items.tease: Next: OpenAI's GPT-6 reaches free users.
items.reelLine: Anthropic cut AI API prices up to 90% this week.

items.title: OpenAI's GPT-6 is now in free ChatGPT accounts
items.body: GPT-6 rolled out to all ChatGPT tiers by October 8. Free accounts get GPT-6 Luna; paid tiers get GPT-6 Sol. The gap between free and paid AI tools keeps narrowing.
items.reelLine: GPT-6 landed in free ChatGPT accounts this week.

items.title: Anthropic targets November IPO; Canadian data centres in motion
items.body: Reports put Anthropic's IPO target at mid-November at approximately $2 trillion. The Logic says it could be a windfall for Canadian investors. Separately, Anthropic confirmed hiring for a Canadian compute country lead to bring gigawatts of capacity online in Canada.
items.reelLine: Anthropic is going public in November at a $2 trillion target.

summary.title: Foreign capital is looking at NWO forestry and the cost of AI just dropped
summary.body: This week: the province backed NWO's forestry accelerator, Scandinavian investors showed up to look at the same resources, and two major AI providers cut their tool costs significantly. The region has a stake in all of it.

captions.carousel: This week in AI and NWO: Ontario put $1.5M into the Boreal Springboard forestry accelerator through the Trade-Impacted Communities Program — up to $40K per entrepreneur. Roughly 50 Scandinavian delegates including Swedish investors came to Thunder Bay to scout the region's poplar and white birch resources. Anthropic cut API prices up to 90% with Claude Haiku 5.5, its new small model built for summarization and classification tasks. OpenAI completed its GPT-6 rollout to all ChatGPT users, including free accounts. And multiple reports say Anthropic is targeting a mid-November IPO at approximately $2 trillion, with confirmed Canadian data centre hiring underway.
